rules: % a premiss as a nullity of two attributes: `All x are y` is `x exists, and no x are not-y`
null(P, X, Y) :- nullity(P, X, Y).
null(P, X, NY) :- every(P, X, Y), neg(Y, NY).
exists(X) :- every(P, X, Y).
% what is null gives an implication each way
imp(X, NY) :- null(P, X, Y), neg(Y, NY).
imp(Y, NX) :- null(P, X, Y), neg(X, NX).
imp(X, Z) :- imp(X, Y), imp(Y, Z).
% an attribute in two premisses is eliminated; one in a single premiss is retained
occurs(P, B) :- null(P, X, Y), base(X, B).
occurs(P, B) :- null(P, X, Y), base(Y, B).
twice(B) :- occurs(P, B), occurs(Q, B), P != Q.
kept(X) :- null(P, X, Y), base(X, B), not twice(B).
kept(Y) :- null(P, X, Y), base(Y, B), not twice(B).
% the conclusion: the two retained attributes are null together
concl(X, Y) :- kept(X), kept(Y), base(X, BX), base(Y, BY), BX != BY, neg(Y, NY), imp(X, NY).
ans_all(X, Y) :- concl(X, Y), exists(X).
some_exists(X, Y) :- concl(X, Y), exists(X).
some_exists(X, Y) :- concl(X, Y), exists(Y).
ans_no(X, Y) :- concl(X, Y), not some_exists(X, Y).
